records.title: feat/agent-orchestration: collected smaller findings from the pre-merge audit
records.body:
Collected while auditing `feat/agent-orchestration` (head `77eb22c`) before it reaches `main`. None of these is a merge blocker on its own; they are grouped here so they do not get lost in the closed PR #8 thread. The bigger items are separate issues, and security-relevant findings went through private vulnerability reporting per SECURITY.md.

The items marked (review) were already listed in https://github.com/vlinx-io/VelaTerm/pull/8#issuecomment-5304152582 and are still open at this head.

## Lifecycle and cleanup

- **(review) Dirty-after-kill retry has no in-product recovery.** `retire --confirm` kills the subtree (`ctl.rs:1316-1325`) and then re-scans (`:1330-1333`); a shutdown write in that window leaves the worktree dirty, and every retry of retire, cleanup and archive re-blocks on "worktree has uncommitted changes" (`ctl.rs:658-662`). Nothing in the product can commit or discard for a killed worker.
- **(review) The running-process guard scans only the archived subtree.** `for worker in &subtree` (`ctl.rs:1138-1166`) never consults a running session outside the subtree whose PTY cwd sits inside an owned worktree, most plausibly the lead itself after `cd`-ing into a child worktree to inspect it. The directory is then removed under a live process, which the guard's own comment at `:1109` says must not happen.
- **(review) Stray keystroke dead-ends retire.** Every write bumps `input_revisions` (`manager.rs:1239-1241`) while `has_current_turn_completion` requires equality (`:219-237`), so one character typed into a waiting worker's pane makes `settle_verdict` return "no current turn-completion signal" (`ctl.rs:953-958`) until a full new agent turn happens. The skill's advice "wait, then run it again" never resolves it.
- **(review) Restore silently re-consumes descendant slots.** Restoring an archived subtree puts it back into `live_descendants` (`repo.rs:859-864`), which the `max_descendants` gate counts. Neither `SKILL.md:134` nor the CLI usage text (`ctl_client.rs:50`) mentions that this can push a lead back over the limit.
- **Failed child creation leaks its worktree and branch.** `executeSpawn` creates the worktree first (`termStore.ts:1841-1852`) and calls `addSession` afterwards (`:1869-1887`). If `addSession` fails, for example on an unknown `--agent` value, the directory and its `vlx/<slug>-<uuid>` branch stay forever and no session row exists, so neither `cleanup` nor `retire` can ever see them.
- **A parked spawn request can stay `pending` forever.** `SPAWN_WAITERS` entries expire only inside `register_spawn_waiter` (`ctl.rs:116-123`), and `op_spawn_status` answers `{"pending":true}` while the entry exists (`:561-580`). If a card is open when the window closes or the webview reloads, `spawn_result` is never called; with no further spawn to trigger the sweep, `vagent spawn-status` reports pending indefinitely.

## Robustness

- **(review) Unclamped `timeoutSecs`** on spawn (`ctl.rs:522-526`), wait (`:280-283`) and the retire card (`:1397-1401`).
- **`vagent read` is uncapped** while `diff` is capped: `op_read` reads the whole transcript with `read_to_string` (`transcript.rs:928-936`) and serializes every message with `--full` (`ctl.rs:332-343`), against `DIFF_PATCH_MAX_BYTES = 256 KB` and `DIFF_COMMIT_MAX = 50` (`ctl.rs:58-59`) for diffs. A multi-hour worker with a large JSONL transcript makes the process hold several copies in memory.
- **Untrusted worker output flows into the lead unmarked.** `op_read` returns worker text as a plain `text` field (`ctl.rs:352-359`) and the skill tells the lead to inspect and act on it, while granting `Bash(vagent:*)`. Nothing marks it as data rather than instructions, and the skill's only injection-adjacent warning is about humans typing into worker panes. A sentence in the skill would help.

## Persistence

- **Parent deletion cascade-erases a surviving worker's landing row.** `agent_landings.parent_session_id` has `ON DELETE CASCADE` (`schema.rs:76`), and `delete_session_node` first rehomes archived workers to `parent_session_id = NULL` (`repo.rs:1417-1421`) and then deletes the parent, so the FK cascade erases the landing evidence of a session that still exists.
- **`worktree_binding_is_shared` ignores archived and tombstoned binders** (`repo.rs:992`, `:995`), while archived sessions keep their `worktree_path` and tombstoned groups are restorable. Archiving a live worker that shares a path with an archived session finds no live sharer, removes the worktree and deletes the branch; restoring the other session then revives a dangling `worktree_path`.
- **`parent_session_id` cycles are accepted.** `move_node` writes the new parent with no ancestry check (`repo.rs:1640-1648`) and is reachable over WS dispatch (`dispatch.rs:386`); only the frontend drag-and-drop guards against it. The feature's own queries are cycle-safe, but the pre-existing `UNION ALL` recursive CTEs (for example `set_archived`, `repo.rs:1762`) have no cycle breaker and would spin while holding the DB mutex.
- **`agent_landings` rows are never deleted on successful retire or cleanup**, so stale verified rows accumulate.

## UI, i18n and docs

- **Backend English strings render raw in new UI surfaces**, against the project rule that backend strings surfacing in the UI go through i18n: launch warnings (`ctl.rs:607-610`) are rendered verbatim at `SpawnConfirmModal.tsx:373-375` under a `status.error` heading although the backend calls them advisory and non-blocking, and the `prepare_archive` refusal text is shown raw by `ArchiveBlocked`.
- **New profiles display the wrong agent.** The panel falls back to `cfg.agent ?? "claude"` (`settingsPanels.tsx:676`), but a profile saved without an agent spawns with the parent's kind (`orchestration.rs:339`, `ctl.rs:586-592`). A Codex lead using such a profile gets a Codex worker while the settings UI showed Claude and Claude's model list.
- **The skip-confirmations warning promises containment the default does not give.** `settings.orchPer

records.title: [RFC]: Specialized Metal Kernel for MLA Paged Attention
records.body:
**Problem:** vllm-metal should support MLA models with the same high-level split used by upstream vLLM: compressed-latent attention for decode, and materialized K/V attention for prefill.

The RFC has moved from pure proposal to implementation tracker. The first two steps have landed: absorbed MLA decode has an opt-in Metal kernel, and absorbed MLA prefill now uses the materialized path by default for pure prefill. The remaining open work is MLA-specific long-context partitioning.

### PR Stack

* [x] PR 1: Absorbed MLA decode kernel behind `VLLM_METAL_MLA_KERNEL=1` (#370). This replaces the earlier draft PR #362.
* [x] PR 2: Materialized prefill for absorbed MLA models (#405).
* [ ] PR 3: MLA long-context partition/reduce decode. #437 landed split-KV decode for regular paged attention, TurboQuant, and sliding-window paths, but MLA decode is explicitly untouched there.
* [ ] Follow-ups: chunked prefill / prefix-cache support, production benchmark grid, docs/support-status update once runtime gates are met, and MLA-specific TurboQuant if the quantization story stabilizes.

### Design

* Keep the existing MLA latent-cache contract; do not fork upstream vLLM scheduling or cache layout.
* Decode follows upstream `forward_mqa`: attend directly over compressed latent K/V.
* Prefill follows upstream `forward_mha`: materialize per-head K/V, then run standard MHA.
* Runtime routing should stay conservative: opt-in or narrowly gated unless wrapper-level parity and production benchmarks justify a wider default.
* Phase 3 should be MLA-specific partition + reduce for long-context decode. Existing split-KV work in #437 is useful reference infrastructure, but not the MLA implementation.
* Performance claims should include wrapper overhead, not just isolated kernel time.

### CC List

@WindChimeRan @LxYuan0420

records.title: Implement build-time component dependency analysis with automatic optimization recommendations
records.body:
## Problem Statement
Vue build systems lack visibility into component dependencies and impact. Large applications have redundant imports and unused dependencies. No automated detection of optimization opportunities. Bundle analysis requires manual effort.

**Business Impact:** Reduces bundle size by 25-40%, improves build times by 30%, accelerates CI/CD pipelines, reduces infrastructure costs.

## Root Cause Analysis
Dependency analysis is post-build. No integrated optimization detection. Developers lack visibility into component dependency graph.

## Solution Overview
Build component dependency analyzer:
- Create build-time dependency graph visualization
- Detect unused imports and dead code
- Identify circular dependencies
- Suggest code-splitting points
- Recommend component extraction opportunities
- Generate optimization reports

**Implementation Steps:**
1. Build dependency graph analyzer
2. Implement graph visualization
3. Create dead code detection
4. Build circular dependency detector
5. Develop optimization recommendation engine

## Type of Change
- Enhancement (build tools)
- Performance optimization
- Developer experience

## Testing Done
- Analyze 50+ Vue applications
- Verify dependency detection accuracy (95%+)
- Performance testing on 10000+ node graphs
- Test circular dependency detection
- Benchmark analysis overhead (< 2 seconds)
- Integration testing with popular build tools
- Validate optimization recommendations

## Related Issues & Standards
- Module graph analysis standards
- Build optimization best practices

## Suggested Labels
- enhancement, build-tools, optimization, tooling, GSSoC26

records.title: Generate benchmark Pareto architecture and lineage explorer
records.body:
<!-- roadmap-key:v19-explorer-dashboard -->
## Summary

Generate a local self-contained explorer for benchmark cells, Pareto fronts, architecture diffs, mutation explanations, experiment lineage, and failures.

## Motivation

This deliverable closes a concrete evidence or capability gap in **v1.9 — Production UX, Ecosystem & Large-Scale Optimization**. It is scoped so downstream issues can consume a versioned, testable result rather than an informal research assumption.

## Scope

- Generate a local self-contained explorer for benchmark cells, Pareto fronts, architecture diffs, mutation explanations, experiment lineage, and failures.
- Produce typed/versioned interfaces, retained evidence, and explicit supported, unsupported, failed, and unknown outcomes where relevant.
- Preserve source models and make cost, hardware, data, configuration, seed, and artifact lineage auditable.

## Non-goals

- A hosted collaborative web service or mutable experiment controller is out of scope.
- Work assigned to direct dependants is excluded from this issue.

## Proposed implementation

Extend deterministic report data into static HTML assets with filters/comparisons, uncertainty/error bars, state/tensor diffs, provenance links and accessibility; embed no remote scripts, secrets or mutable queries and handle large campaigns via bounded generated partitions.

Implementation must use the owning `area:explainability` boundary, bounded resources, deterministic identifiers, explicit compatibility checks, and safe resume/rollback behavior where persistent artifacts are changed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every displayed value is a projection of canonical evidence and links its immutable source.
- [ ] Unsupported/failed/negative cells remain visible and distinguishable from missing data.
- [ ] Explorer works offline, passes accessibility smoke checks, and scales to at least 100k cells within declared generation/browser bounds.

## Benchmark / research protocol

Use golden small reports plus a synthetic 100k-cell campaign and real v1.1-v1.7 bundles; test deterministic rendering, XSS/path redaction, accessibility, browser performance and data reconciliation.

For research-bearing work, preregister exact model families/checkpoints and revisions, datasets/tasks/splits and licenses, baselines/ablations, hardware and optimization/evaluation budgets, metrics and decision thresholds, random seeds, repeated-run confidence intervals, failure/unsupported-cell retention, and complete code/config/tool/artifact provenance. Do not turn a negative or inconclusive result into a success claim.

## Tests

- [ ] Add unit tests for records, validation and deterministic decisions; integration tests for direct dependencies and public interfaces; regression tests for prior supported behavior; and real-artifact tests on licensed tiny fixtures or declared representative models when applicable.
- [ ] Exercise success, invalid-input, unsupported, interrupted/resumed, and negative-result paths relevant to this deliverable.
- [ ] Run the repository quality gate and record exact commands, environment, revisions, outcomes, and known skips.

## Documentation impact

- Update the applicable architecture/design document and public command/API/schema documentation.
- Add or update a research report with protocol, full results, negative cells, limitations, and reproduction commands when evidence is collected.
- Update `CHANGELOG.md`, compatibility tables, examples, and migration guidance for user-visible changes.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- #191
- #367
- #383
- #417

Blocks:
- #421

Dependency keys: `report-generator, v12-physical-pareto-study, v14-architecture-pareto-study, v19-registry-cli`.

## Risks

- Project risk: **Medium**. Effort: **L**. Priority: **P1**.
- Primary risks include overfitting, benchmark leakage, unsupported-format assumptions, resource overruns, non-reproducible measurements, and misleading extrapolation; applicability depends on this issue's scope.
- Mitigate with held-out cells, hard budgets, compatibility gates, immutable evidence, confidence reporting, failure retention, and explicit claim boundaries.

## Completion evidence

- [ ] Static explorer generator, visual/golden tests, accessibility/performance report, and example site exist.
- [ ] Link implementation commits/PRs, test and benchmark logs, retained manifests/artifacts, documentation, and any negative or inconclusive results.
- [ ] Verify every acceptance item against the merged commit; prose, mock-only output, or an unreviewed local branch is not completion evidence.

records.title: lib: add process-rooted closure analysis for inherited DT_RPATH
records.body:
# lib: add process-rooted closure analysis for inherited DT_RPATH

## Problem

The current analyzer treats every package-owned ELF object as an independent consumer.

For each object, it compiles a resolver plan from:

* that object’s own `DT_RPATH` or `DT_RUNPATH`;
* explicit process search directories;
* configured and default directories;
* package-local extension directories.

This is appropriate for package-wide edge auditing, but it cannot model one important part of runtime-loader behavior:

* `DT_RUNPATH` applies only to the direct dependencies of the object carrying it;
* `DT_RPATH`, when not superseded by `DT_RUNPATH`, may remain available while resolving descendants in the dependency closure.

Correct resolution may therefore depend on the executable or shared object from which loading began.

The same shared object can resolve a dependency differently under two different process roots. A report keyed only by consumer object and `DT_NEEDED` name cannot represent that distinction.

## Target

Add a separate process-rooted closure-analysis interface that traverses dependency graphs from explicit entry objects and carries inherited loader context through the traversal.

The existing package-wide `analyzer::run()` interface should remain available with its current edge-local meaning.

## Proposed direction

Introduce a distinct analysis operation rather than silently changing the semantics of existing reports.

A possible public shape is:

```cpp
struct closure_request {
  std::vector<object_path> entry_objects;
  target_profile target;
};

closure_report closure_analyzer::run(
    const inventory& consumers,
    const provider_ownership& ownership,
    const resolver_config& resolver,
    elf_backend& backend,
    closure_request request) const;
```

Each traversal node needs enough context to distinguish:

* the entry object that began the closure;
* the current consumer object;
* inherited `DT_RPATH` directories;
* the resolved provider path;
* the dependency name;
* observation failures encountered under that closure.

The resolver context should evolve as follows:

* an object with `DT_RUNPATH` uses it for its direct dependencies but does not pass it to children;
* an object with `DT_RPATH` and no `DT_RUNPATH` contributes its expanded RPATH to descendant resolution;
* explicit process, configured, cache, default, and package-local inputs remain caller-controlled;
* `DF_1_NODEFLIB`, target profiles, hwcaps ordering, and provider compatibility continue to apply normally.

## Invariants

* Results depend only on explicit caller-supplied facts.
* The library does not inspect the running process environment.
* The library does not execute the entry object.
* Traversal order does not affect report ordering.
* Dependency cycles terminate deterministically.
* Repeated objects may be revisited when their inherited resolver context differs.
* Candidate observations remain reusable within one analysis run.
* Provider ownership remains independent of consumer selection.
* Incomplete observations remain distinct from unresolved dependencies.

## Report identity

A closure finding must not collapse two edges merely because they share:

```text
consumer object + DT_NEEDED name
```

The finding identity must also retain the process root or equivalent resolver context when that context can change the selected provider.

For example:

```text
/app/a -> /usr/lib/libchild.so -> libprivate.so
/app/b -> /usr/lib/libchild.so -> libprivate.so
```

may legitimately select different providers when `/app/a` and `/app/b` establish different inherited RPATH state.

## Non-goals

* Do not replace the existing package-wide linkage analyzer.
* Do not model `dlopen()`, `dlmopen()`, or arbitrary runtime namespaces initially.
* Do not model symbol lookup, interposition, relocation, constructors, or ABI versioning in this issue.
* Do not infer entry objects from package metadata.
* Do not read ambient `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.
* Do not add package-manager transaction policy to the library.

## Acceptance criteria

* An entry executable’s `DT_RPATH` can resolve a grandchild dependency.
* The same executable’s `DT_RUNPATH` cannot resolve that grandchild unless the intermediate object supplies its own applicable path.
* `DT_RUNPATH` suppresses the same object’s `DT_RPATH`.
* Two entry objects can produce different provider resolutions for the same child object and needed name.
* Cyclic dependency graphs terminate and produce deterministic reports.
* Shared subgraphs are reused when their resolver context is equivalent.
* Different inherited contexts are not incorrectly merged.
* Missing and malformed observations preserve report incompleteness.
* Existing `analyzer::run()` behavior and tests remain unchanged.
* The new semantics are documented in `libpkgimpact(3)` and `pkgimpact(7)`.

records.title: foxy rebuilds a 256x256 volumetric field ~24x/second on the main thread — two CI observations, and gating the tick is REFUSED (#1720/#1721)
records.body:
`foxy`'s bridge recomputes a **256×256 volumetric heightfield and rescans it into a 64×256 wavetable ~24×/second, on the page main thread**, for as long as any surface is displaying the module. It has now cost two CI observations, and it is the reason foxy needed the first-ever `FACE_QUIESCE` entry (#2041).

## The mechanism

`foxy.ts`'s `bridgeTick()` runs inside the engine handle's `read()` seam. Per tick (throttled to `BRIDGE_MS = 42`, so ~24 Hz):

- three `RasterPainter.paint()` calls over a 256×256 buffer,
- `boxHeightfield3d(imgA, imgB, imgC, 256, 256)` — 65 536 cells,
- `boxToField3d(...)` — another full pass, with bilinear sampling and a blur whose radius is `round(smooth*8)`,
- `fieldToWavetable(...)` → 64×256,
- a `wavetableSignature()` fingerprint over the result.

The video stages are pure CPU **by design** and that design is sound — the header explains it: foxy is an AUDIO def, the audio engine has no GL context, and standing up a private VideoEngine inside an audio node would be heavy and fragile. This issue is not a proposal to move it to the GPU.

## The two observations

Both on PR #2041's CI runs, both on `faces-parity`'s foxy row, which drives 33 cells and makes a Playwright round trip per cell **on the same main thread**:

1. **Recovered on retry** — a flake the fail-on-flaky gate caught (#1847).
2. **Failed both attempts** — `Test timeout of 144000ms exceeded`, stopped at the drag-commit `expect.poll` partway through the cell walk. The runner class measured **1.30 rAF/s**.

⚠ **The budget was already the right shape.** `faces-parity` derives its timeout as `FACE_FIXED_MS + FACE_PER_CELL_MS * cells.length` — already per-cell, already 3 s/cell under `SLOW_RENDER` — and 45 s + 3 s × 33 **is** the 144 s that blew. So this was never a case of a flat budget being too small.

## What #2041 did, and what it did not

It added a generic per-def quiesce hook to `faces-parity` and foxy adopts it through `__foxyVrtSeed`, the determinism seed the module already carries: `bridgeTick` paints once from fixed synthetic waveforms and short-circuits thereafter. Measured locally under `E2E_SWIFTSHADER=1`: **~60 s unquiesced → 46.4/46.7/47.2 s quiesced** across a 3× flake-check.

That makes the *test* affordable. **It does not make the module cheaper for a player**, who gets the full recompute whenever a foxy faceplate or card is open. That is what this issue is for.

## ⚠ Gating the tick is REFUSED — do not "fix" it that way

The obvious move — skip `bridgeTick` when the preview is collapsed or off-screen — is the **#1720 / #1721 class** and must not be taken. `bridgeTick` is *pull-driven*: it runs inside `read()`, so when nothing downstream is patched, **the open surface's render loop is the only thing advancing the rasters and the table**. Gating it would freeze the instrument itself, not just its picture — the owner's stated floor for SCREEN OFF is that the module *keeps rendering*. #2041's `FoxyOutputBody` is explicit about this: it throttles the **blits** and never the tick, and `foxy-face-model.test.ts` asserts the tick sits before the collapse branch at source precisely so this cannot be undone by accident.

## Directions that do not have that problem

Unexplored, listed so the next person does not start at zero:

- **Dirty-tracking**: the field only changes when a raster changed. `wavetableSignature` already fingerprints the *output*; fingerprinting the three raster inputs would let `boxToField3d` + `fieldToWavetable` be skipped when all three are frozen (all four `freeze*` toggles on is the degenerate case, and today it still recomputes).
- **Resolution**: `FOXY_FIELD_SIZE = 256` is used for both the painted raster and the scanned field. Whether the *scan* needs full resolution is a question the module can answer; the wavetable it feeds is 64×256.
- **Incremental paint**: each tick paints a fixed run of samples and the cursors drift, so most of the 65 536 cells are unchanged between ticks.

Any of these is a behaviour change to a live audio path and wants its own ART/attest consideration, which is why it is filed rather than folded into a face PR.

Filed from #2041 (foxy faceplate).

records.title: pages: trash cascade implemented twice, plus raw non-cascading writers — the class of bug repair-orphaned-trashed-pages.ts fixes can recur
records.body:
## What

"This subtree is trashed" is stored N times — every page carries its own `isTrashed`/`trashedAt` (`schema/core.ts:45,87`), `pages.parentId` has no FK (`core.ts:91`), and consistency depends entirely on app-level recursion. That recursion exists in **two independent implementations**, and several writers skip it entirely:

**Cascade implementations (duplicated logic)**
- `apps/web/src/services/api/page-service.ts:286-322` `recursivelyTrash` (canonical)
- `apps/web/src/lib/ai/tools/page-write-tools.ts:233-278` — its own copy (withChildren recursion / move-children-up), mirroring pageService by hand

**Non-cascading raw writers (the drift generators)**
- `packages/lib/src/repositories/page-repository.ts:222-245` (`trash`, `trashMany` — single-level)
- `lib/integrations/google-calendar/sync-service.ts:319,505` — direct `db.update(pages).set({isTrashed:true})`
- `lib/machines/machine-settings-runtime.ts:147`
- `api/pages/[pageId]/tasks/[taskId]/route.ts:560` — trashes a single task page even though task pages can have children

**Proof the drift class is real**: `scripts/repair-orphaned-trashed-pages.ts` — "Historically, trashing a page did NOT trash its children … those live descendants surfaced as bogus top-level items" — a recursive-CTE repair script. Any of the remaining non-cascading writers can recreate exactly the bug that script repairs.

## Proposed direction

One cascade, one owner: move `recursivelyTrash` into the shared service/repository layer, have the AI tool call it instead of maintaining a copy, and make the raw single-level writers either call the cascade or be renamed to make their non-cascading nature impossible to reach for by accident (`trashSinglePageUnsafe`). Alternatively, derive trash state at read time from the nearest trashed ancestor (recursive CTE / closure table), so subtree-trash is stored **once** and the repair script class disappears entirely.

---
Filed from the sources-of-truth audit.

records.title: [Bug]: install --dry-run omits installed database state and produces a misleading dependency plan
records.body:
### Summary

When running dbpm install --dry-run with valid database connection settings, dbpm does not query Core for installed package state.
As a result, dependencies already installed at compatible versions appear in execution_order as fresh database installations. This can make the dry-run plan materially different from the plan used by the corresponding real installation.

### Reproduction steps

Example
Given:
JOB_CONTROL 1.1.0 is installed with deployment status C.
The root package declares:
dependencies:
  - name: job_control
    version: "^1.1.0"
Run:
source ~/.config/dbpm/app_x/environments/development.sh

dbpm install . \
  --dry-run \
  --dependency-source ../job_control
The resulting plan includes:
{
  "execution_order": [
    "JOB_CONTROL",
    "UNIVERSAL_FILE_LOADER"
  ]
}
The JOB_CONTROL package plan also reports:
{
  "installed_state": null,
  "mode": "install"
}
A direct query of Core metadata confirms:
JOB_CONTROL 1.1.0 C
The non-dry-run install path does query installed state and should treat JOB_CONTROL as a satisfied dependency rather than redeploying its database objects.
Expected behavior
When database connectivity is available, dbpm install --dry-run should query installed state and produce the same dependency resolution and execution order that the real install would use.
Expected plan characteristics:
{
  "execution_order": [
    "UNIVERSAL_FILE_LOADER"
  ],
  "satisfied_dependencies": [
    {
      "application_name": "JOB_CONTROL",
      "installed_state": {
        "version": "1.1.0",
        "deploy_status": "C"
      }
    }
  ]
}
The application runtime plan may still include the job_control runtime payload for composition into the target runtime prefix.
Actual behavior
install --dry-run unconditionally omits installed-state lookup. The resulting output appears to show that dbpm will execute the dependency’s initial database deployment, even though the real install will resolve it as already satisfied.
This is especially concerning for dependencies whose initial deployment scripts recreate tables or otherwise assume a clean installation.
Impact
Dry-run output does not accurately preview the real installation.
Operators may unnecessarily uninstall an existing dependency.
Operators may avoid a safe install because the plan appears destructive.
CI approval workflows cannot reliably use the dry-run JSON as the proposed execution plan.
The distinction between database deployment and runtime-payload composition is unclear.
Suggested resolution
Preferably, when database connection settings are available, make install --dry-run load installed state using the same path as the real installation.
If retaining database-independent dry runs is intentional, consider:
Adding an explicit option such as --offline or --ignore-installed-state.
Emitting a prominent warning:
WARNING: Dry-run did not query installed database state. Satisfied dependencies
may appear as new installations, and execution_order may differ from a real
install.
Adding plan metadata such as:
{
  "installed_state_evaluated": false,
  "execution_order_is_provisional": true
}
Documenting that dbpm plan --mode install with database access must be used to obtain an installed-state-aware preview.
Environment
dbpm 1.4.2
Oracle Database
Core deployment metadata enabled
Structured connection settings:
DBPM_DB_USER
DBPM_DB_PASSWORD
DBPM_DB_DSN

### Environment

- dbpm version:
- Python version:
- Oracle version:
- SQL runner: SQLcl / SQL*Plus / other
- Operating system:


### Workflow

check-core

### Logs or output

```text

```

records.title: Dijkstra experiment: audit state-machine and concurrency correctness
records.body:
## Worker

Experimental worker: **Dijkstra**

Marker: `VOID_WORKER_DIJKSTRA_STATE_MACHINE_CORRECTNESS_EXPERIMENT_V1`

## Mission

Find and close bounded correctness gaps in state machines, asynchronous control flow, retries, timers, idempotence, and exact transition authority without duplicating an occupied implementation lane.

Dijkstra should prefer small, formally explainable repairs that make invalid states unrepresentable or fail closed. The goal is not broad refactoring; it is to identify where stale evidence, race windows, ambiguous terminal states, replay, timeout conflation, or partial mutation could produce a result the repository cannot truthfully justify.

## First bounded lane

Begin read-only and produce an evidence-backed correctness audit that:

- inventories high-risk state machines and asynchronous transition seams outside current Red lanes;
- checks exact preconditions, terminal-state closure, retry/idempotence behavior, timer ownership, stale-object binding, and partial-failure handling;
- distinguishes a concrete reachable defect from stylistic complexity or speculative concern;
- records exact files, transitions, triggering conditions, current tests, and authority consequences;
- ranks at most three candidates by core impact, reachability, reproducibility, repair size, regression risk, and proofability; and
- recommends only one candidate for a later source repair after a fresh current-main/open-PR/recent-write collision check.

The first report must explicitly avoid the frozen Moe descendant stack and any actively occupied `src/node_core.ts`, consensus, economic-mutation, deployment, wallet, signer, validator, or Work Credit lane.

## Non-idle exploration rule

When no confirmed correctness repair is safely actionable, Dijkstra remains in bounded read-only exploration rather than inventing a refactor. Exploration output is limited to this issue and at most one draft PR. Duplicate state machines, architecture churn, whole-file rewrites, and cosmetic type cleanup without a proven behavioral gain are rejected.

## Boundaries

Read-only audit first. No live fault injection, denial of service, production probing, deployment, service mutation, credential or secret access, router/firewall/DNS/interface change, wallet/signer use, validator action, Work Credit mutation, transaction, treasury action, liquidity action, or funds movement.

Any source mutation requires a fresh V1 Red/Amber/Green check, a bounded branch, exact adversarial regression proof, and a draft pull request. Ready-for-review and merge remain separate gates.

Doctrine: **Protect the Core. Protect the Truth. Protect the Sovereign.**

Coordination source of truth: #1182 and the checked-in `AGENTS.md` agreement.

records.title: Helm leg-one 03: S2 - owner projection envelopes for the organism regions
records.body:
## Parent
Wayfinder MAP #1277 via spec PR #1399 (`docs/plans/helm_legone/HELM_LEGONE_SPEC.md`), §3 obligation 7 (S2+S3 of the self-awareness contract) and §5.4 (order after ticket one); ruling #1386 (Slices 2–5 resolution).

## What to build
Give every organism region the Helm can show — MissionControl, TaskBoard, RuntimeState, Swarm, A2A, and evolution — a real, honest "envelope" around its data: each region's display must be backed by an actual owner (the real subsystem that knows that region's truth), must say how fresh that data is, must say if it disagrees with another source (divergence), and must say plainly "unknown" when it doesn't know, rather than silently showing nothing or showing stale data as if it were current.

This is data plumbing only. The visual redesign of these regions (S4/S5, the "recursive Inspector") is explicitly excluded from leg one (spec §3 obligation 7) — this ticket only makes sure each region's envelope is real and honestly labeled.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each of the six organism regions (MissionControl, TaskBoard, RuntimeState, Swarm, A2A, evolution) is bound to a real owner adapter that declares its freshness clock, its partial/stale/unavailable semantics, and ships a deterministic fixture (spec §4.1 obligation B, the Adapter gate). Verifier: for each region, a test exercises that region's adapter against its fixture and asserts the freshness/partial/stale/unavailable states are distinguishable in the output.
- [ ] No owner adapter mutates state on a read. Verifier: call each adapter's read path twice against the same fixture and assert byte-identical output both times — the "no side effects on read" half of the Adapter gate.
- [ ] The Protocol v2 envelope fields (`schema_version`, `correlation_id`/`causation_id`/`parent_id`, monotonic sequence, attachment digest — spec §4.1 obligation A) are present on every owner projection, and the same golden vectors pass in both the TypeScript and Python implementations. Verifier: the shared golden-vector test suite (Protocol gate, spec §6) run on both sides.
- [ ] Negative control: feed one owner adapter a fixture representing a genuinely stale or unavailable upstream (e.g. a runtime status source that hasn't reported in longer than its freshness window) and confirm the envelope reports `stale`/`unavailable`, never silently `fresh`/`ok`. A projection that reports fresh data from a stale fixture must fail this check.

## Blocked by
#1402 (Helm leg-one 02: Ink 5.1 to 7 migration) — S2 lands after Ink 7 per spec §5.4.
